title: Tech Note: File Transfers using Execute on Server
author: Timothy Aaron Penner, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: Execute on Server method property (4D v11 SQL Release 2), a 'twin process' alternative to the Execute on Server command
GFFS (Get Files from Server) sample: chunked BLOB file transfer using READ PACKET/SEND PACKET
Manual multipart BLOB protocol with custom header bytes for chunk numbering
4D Client/Server automatic parameter and dereferenced-pointer synchronization

historical_commentary.text: This note explains the Execute on Server method property (introduced in 4D v11 SQL Release 2) as a simpler alternative to the Execute on Server command, and applies it to a hand-built chunked file-transfer scheme (GFFS) that manually splits large files into blobs with custom header bytes to work around then-current transfer size practicalities. The Execute on Server method property itself remains a current, fully supported 4D Server feature for delegating logic to the server in Client/Server mode. However, the GFFS file-chunking technique is a manual workaround for limitations in transferring large binary data between client and server that has been substantially reduced by later improvements to 4D's client/server networking and blob/document handling, and a modern implementation would likely rely on built-in document transfer facilities, REST endpoints, or newer client/server APIs rather than a hand-rolled multipart blob protocol.
related_updates: The Execute on Server method property remains a current 4D Server feature unchanged in principle since this note
4D's client/server networking and file/document handling have significantly improved since 2009, reducing the need for the hand-built chunked-blob transfer protocol (GFFS) shown here
REST server + ORDA (4D v16 R5+, 2017) offers an additional, more modern channel for transferring data/files between client and server tiers
